newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-FLEMING LEADS NEW ZEALAND FIGHTBACK WITH UNBEATEN 52.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-FLEMING LEADS NEW ZEALAND FIGHTBACK WITH UNBEATEN 52.

text.p: Stephen Fleming led New Zealand's fightback with a fluent unbeaten half century after they had slumped to 110 for six on the opening day of the second test against Pakistan on Thursday.
Fleming, with nine fours in his 52, carried the touring team to 163 for seven at tea.
Debutant Mohammad Zahir, a right-arm fast medium bowler, and leg spinner Mushtaq Ahmed were the men who inflicted most of the damage.
Zahir, who dismissed opener Justin Vaughan and Adam Parore in the morning session, followed up after lunch with the wicket of Chris Harris. All three were trapped leg before.

Mushtaq, bowling unchanged throughout the afternoon, had Nathan Astle caught behind by Moin Khan for 10 and then tempted Mark Greatbatch into a heave. Skipper Saeed Anwar took an easy catch at long-off.
Mushtaq had claimed the important scalp of Bryan Young shortly before lunch when the opener looked set for a big score. He was leg before for 39.
